part.text:
Fixed CVE-2024-39338 with a single change in lib/helpers/isAbsoluteURL.js:

- **Root cause:** the `schemeRelativePattern` `/^([a-z][a-z\d+\-.]*:)?\/\//i` treated scheme-less protocol-relative URLs (`//google.com`) as absolute, so `buildFullPath` returned them untouched instead of joining them with `baseURL`; the http adapter then resolved them against `http://localhost`, enabling SSRF.
- **Fix:** the pattern now requires an explicit scheme (`/^([a-z][a-z\d+\-.]*):\/\//i`), and the redundant `origin.href` check was dropped, so a protocol-relative request URL is combined with the baseURL.

Validation:
- FAIL_TO_PASS: `test/unit/regression/SNYK-JS-AXIOS-7361793.js` (SSRF) now passes — the request goes to `http://localhost:<good>/localhost:<bad>` and never reaches the bad server.
- PASS_TO_PASS: full mocha unit suite 188 passing (only pre-existing network-dependent `should support HTTPS protocol` timeout, which also fails on the pristine baseline), both SSRF regression tests, and all 312 karma browser specs pass. ESLint clean; no test files modified.
